verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch from the github-actions vantage (28 resource types, fhirVersion 4.0.1); base URL published in Capital Blue Cross's own Patient Access API access guide. endpoints.name: Inland Empire Health Plan Patient Access API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 17 resource types); publisher field reads 'IEHP' and implementation description 'FHIR Endpoint powered by Smile CDR' on an IEHP-controlled domain. Base URL printed as 'FHIR Server Base URL' on IEHP's own Swagger page at https://fhir.iehp.org/fhir-request/swagger-ui/?page=All, reached from the plan's developer portal at https://www.iehp.org/devportal/index.html

endpoints.name: Inland Empire Health Plan Provider Directory API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 7 resource types); publisher field reads 'IEHP' and implementation description 'IEHP Provider Directory - FHIR Endpoint' on an IEHP-controlled domain. IEHP's developer portal describes it as 'a publicly available standards-based open API', which matches the Provider Directory API requirement to be reachable without authentication

endpoints.name: Sharp Health Plan Patient Access API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 24 resource types); publisher field reads 'Sharp Health Plan', title 'Patient Access APIs Reference Implementation', software 'SHP Patient APIs' on a Sharp Health Plan controlled domain. Base URL and capability-statement URL published on Sharp's own public Anypoint Exchange portal, linked from https://www.sharphealthplan.com/api-access-for-developers

endpoints.name: Sharp Health Plan Provider Directory API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 7 Plan-Net resource types); publisher field reads 'Sharp Health Plan', title 'Da Vinci Payer Data exchange Plan Network Reference Implementation'. Sharp's portal documents this base URL and states the directory 'does not require authorization to access the data on the server'. Its implementation.url advertises a different path (/providerdirectory/api) which answers 401, so this entry records the documented base that answers rather than the one the document names

endpoints.name: Kaiser Permanente Health Plan Patient Access API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 10 resource types including Coverage and ExplanationOfBenefit); publisher field reads 'Kaiser Permanente' and implementation description 'FHIR Endpoint powered by Smile CDR' on a kp.org domain. Sourced from ONC's Lantern endpoint export, which records the list source as Kaiser's own developer portal at https://developer.kp.org/#/apis/639c015049655aa96ab5b2f1. This is the health-plan surface; the Kaiser endpoints listed under open.epic.com are the care-delivery side and are not this entry

endpoints.name: Santa Clara Family Health Plan Provider Directory API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 4 resource types); publisher 'Not provided', implementation description 'FHIR Endpoint powered by SCFHP' on the scfhp.com domain, base URL published in the plan's own developer documentation

endpoints.name: Health Plan of San Mateo Patient Access API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 144 resource types). The CapabilityStatement names the vendor, not the plan: publisher '1upHealth', software '1up FHIR Server'. Attribution to Health Plan of San Mateo rests on the plan printing this base URL on its own site, at https://www.hpsm.org/about-us/data-interoperability/app-developer-resources, under the heading 'Available Patient Access and Provider Directory API Endpoints'. The same base URL appears in ONC's Lantern export via the 1upHealth endpoint directory. One base serves both surfaces per the plan's own heading

endpoints.name: L.A. Care Health Plan Provider Directory API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 24 resource types); implementation.url matches the requested base exactly. The document names no organization at all: publisher reads 'Not provided' and software is a generic 'HAPI FHIR Server' with an Edifecs build suffix (5.4.1.11_edfx) on an Edifecs-controlled host. Attribution to L.A. Care rests entirely on the plan publishing this exact string as its 'PROD Base/Endpoint URL' at https://lacare.org/technical-information, never on the 'lac' path segment

endpoints.name: Central California Alliance for Health Provider Directory API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 24 resource types); implementation.url matches the requested base exactly, which is what confirms the base. Publisher reads 'Not provided' and software is a generic 'HAPI FHIR Server' (5.4.1.13_edfx) on an Edifecs-controlled host, so the document names nobody. Attribution to the Alliance rests on its own published Provider Directory API documentation PDF, linked from https://thealliance.health/about-the-alliance/developer-resources/, whose worked example requests and response self-links are resource URLs under this base

endpoints.name: Community Health Group Provider Directory API

verification.method: live CapabilityStatement fetch (fhirVersion 4.0.1, 8 Plan-Net resource types). The document identifies no deployment: it is the Da Vinci PDex Plan-Net implementation guide's own CapabilityStatement served verbatim, with publisher 'HL7 Financial Management Working Group' and the canonical hl7.org url. Attribution to Community Health Group rests on the plan publishing this exact capability-statement URL at https://www.chgsd.com/about-us/fhir-developer-api; the host is the Onyx SAFHIR platform
